Layers 6 and 7 exclude category O ('a separate development and are not assumed here'). No atlas stage plans category O, Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, the Kazhdan–Lusztig theorem or D-modules. Route 1's brief, 'Import category O, Verma modules and Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials from the Tau Ceti representation-theory roadmaps', therefore imports from nowhere. The quotations on pp. 320–321 match. Corrections. (a) An accepted route already proposes algebraic category O: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25 route 3, a part-ii of LieHighestWeight (LieHighestWeightPartIICompletedCategoryO), whose brief notes that 'Upstream LieHighestWeight explicitly excludes full category O'. The same assumption in PAPER-DING-25's route 1 brief is a note for the maintainer.

Confirmed, and high is right: stated results carry a false number. I redid the count from the paper's own dimensions, with d = [K:Q_p]. Spec Ô_{𝔛_r̄,r} has dimension n² + dn² (p. 377). X_tri(r̄) has dimension n² + d·n(n+1)/2 (p. 365). The weight fibre Spec R_{r,M•} has codimension d·n(n+1)/2 (p. 379). The character space T_L of K^× has dimension d + 1, so the fibre T^n_{L,wt(δ)} of wt, over which (4.11) is taken (p. 382), has dimension n(d + 1) − dn = n. Hence the character fibre has codimension d·n(n+1)/2 + n and dimension n² − n + d·n(n−1)/2, equivalently dim X_tri(r̄) − dim T^n_L. The printed values are codimension d·n(n+3)/2 = d·n(n+1)/2 + dn (Theorem 1.9 on p. 305, Conjecture 4.3.4 on p. 381, the cycle groups of (4.11)–(4.12) on p. 382) and fibre dimension n² + d·n(n−3)/2 (Remark 4.3.5). These agree with the corrected values only for d = 1. The check n = 1, d = 2 is decisive. The ring has dimension 3, and the fibre over δ is a point, of codimension 3, while the printed codimension is 4 and the printed fibre dimension is −1. The same n(n+3) is in arXiv v1. §5 is unaffected: p. 399 uses only weight fibres, with codimension [F⁺:Q]·n(n+1)/2. Correction to the claim: three items state the number, 1-thm19-breuil-mezard, 4.3-cycles-setup and 4.3.4-conjecture (whose note also has the fibre dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n−3)/2), together with conventions.cycles and the gap two-cycle-families. 4.3.7-independence and 4.3.8-theorem only refer to the cycles 4.3-cycles-setup defines, so they inherit it. The fix stands: E12 as proposed, and the corrected codimension wherever the number is stated.

Confirmed. p. 315 prints: 'Let f : Y → Z be a morphism of noetherian schemes and assume that Z is regular and Y is Cohen-Macaulay. Assume that the fibers of f are equidimensional of dimension dim Y − dim Z. Then f is flat.' The counterexample works. Y = Spec k ⊔ A¹_k maps to Z = A¹_k, with the isolated point going to 0. Every fibre has dimension 0 = dim Y − dim Z, but k[t]_(t) → k, t ↦ 0, is not flat. The proof uses the local equality 'dim S/(f1, …, fd)S = dim S − d', which the global hypothesis does not give. The equality does follow when Y is equidimensional and of finite type over a field and Z is irreducible: both sides equal dim Y − dim cl{f(y)} − trdeg(κ(y)/κ(f(y))). Every use in the paper satisfies it: κ_{i,w} on the irreducible X_w (p. 316), and f₁ on V_w (p. 317). On p. 408 the lemma is applied to the spectra of local rings, where the hypothesis at the closed fibre is exactly the local equality. So 'affects nothing' is right. Medium fits: item 2.3.2-miracle-flatness is false as written, but the fix is a hypothesis change that every use meets. The fix stands. (The finding's 'Matsumoto, Theorem 23.1' is Matsumura's Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 23.1.)

Confirmed. p. 337 requires the graded pieces of a filtered A⊗_{Q_p}K-representation of G_a to be 'free of rank 1 over A ⊗_{Q_p} K for i ∈ Z'. E8 corrects this to 'free over A⊗_{Q_p}K', and the review confirmed that correction ('"free" is what is meant, rank zero included'). But each gr^i splits into τ-components, and it is free over L⊗_{Q_p}K ≅ ∏_τ L only if dim gr^i_τ does not depend on τ. A rank-one object with non-parallel weights k = (k_τ) has its τ-jump at −k_τ, so gr^{−k_τ} is non-zero in the τ-slot alone. The paper handles such τ-dependent jumps throughout: (3.9) is 'Fil_{W⁺_A,i} := ⊕_τ Fil^{−h_{τ,i}}', and p. 340 draws from Lemma 3.2.2 that the τ-components 'are all free A-modules of finite type'. The proof's criterion, which E8's reason quotes ('finite free over A⊗K'), concerns the whole of gr^•, not each gr^i. So with E8's correction Lemma 3.2.2's equivalence would not be essentially surjective. The error has reached research/errata/REGISTER.md, which lists E8 among the confirmed new mistakes with this correction. The fix stands: 'finite projective A⊗_{Q_p}K-modules'. The red team's gloss 'i.e. τ-components free over A' holds for A in C_L, which is the case the paper uses. E8's rank-one sentence is dropped, and item 3.2.2-filtered-equivalence is restated to match.

Confirmed. (a) The proof of Proposition 2.3.3 (p. 316) reaches only the generic-fibre points that specialise to the special fibre, and X_A is not proper over A, since its g-factor is affine. The G_m-scaling repair works, and the paper uses the same limit argument in Lemma 2.3.1 (p. 315). (b) The proof of Proposition 3.7.2 (pp. 366–367) fixes one x̃. Injectivity on complete local rings fails where U has several branches, as k[[a,b]]/(ab) → k[[t]] shows. Local irreducibility comes only later, in Corollary 3.7.10, which depends on this proposition. Using all points of f⁻¹(x) repairs it, since S is reduced and f is proper and birational. The fix stands. Items have no proof field, so the repairs go into the notes of 2.3.3-cm-flat and 3.7.3-closed-immersion.
